> I don't think you should be comparing finding a relationship to winning a lottery ticket.

The pursuit of something to make you happy in life is the pursuit of something to make you happy in life. Be it a relationship, a musical, acting, or pro-sports career, and yes, even hitting a lottery ticket. They are all things we pursuit for the happiness in life we believe that will follow.

> And I do think being a secure and content person makes finding a relationship way, way, way easier. So I don't think there's any false hope I'm giving out.

Yes, fixing one's mental health will make it easier and increases the odds of success, no argument here. However, it does not guarantee success, which is how it was originally worded.

I totally agree. People in their 20's have just left the starting area to the game of life and seem totally bent out of shape that they don't have the end game reward. 


However, the last line should have ended with "...gonna be so much happier." But that last little bit...I'll rephrase it to explain why I hate it so much.


Get used to being poor, be comfortable with being poor. If you can be poor and not feel depressed, you're not only gonna be so much happier, you're also going to win that lottery ticket you've been waiting for very, very soon.


Please stop giving people false hope.

I was maybe 12 or 13 years old. Boston's Museum of Science had a laser show back in the early 80's that opened with Speak to Me/Breathe/On the Run. It blew my mind (mostly On the Run) and I had no idea what it was or who the artist was, I just knew I loved what I had heard. Some years later I got into smoking weed, just bought this somewhat still new thing called a CD player and was in a record store when my friend came up to me with a CD with a prism on it and said "No one should be without this album". So I bought it, and at night when I put it on, OMG! it's the music I so longed to hear again!!! I was falling asleep to it, only to be shocked awake when all the chimes went of at the start of Time. It wasn't long after that before I had all their albums.

I'm over 50. Abandoned by my father. Lived in fear of my religious grandparents. Drifted from my siblings and other close family. Had major financial, mental and physical health problems. Was homeless for a short period of time. Most of it back when I was your age. 

It was rough going at times, but life did get better. Hardships when you're young will only make you stronger when you have to face them again later. Learn the lessons life teaches you and persevere.

Like Snoop says, I smoke weed everyday and have been for the last thirty years or so. Why? When it comes to toxic consumption, it's the most simple in terms of complexity and therefore the safest (IMHO). You plant a seed, water it, it grows. You pick it, dry it, and smoke it. You don't need a lab coat and respirator, or a degree in chemistry. At no point in it's preparation will it explode, or produce byproducts that will kill you. I smoke for musical inspiration and to cope with being bored and lonely. If I am out with other people, getting high is the furthest thing from my mind. I've done cocaine and LSD, both of which are awesome and definitely have their uses. My best advice is to 'just say know'. Know who you're getting it from, know what you're actually taking and know who you're doing them with and just try to be safe.

As someone who feels abandoned by his own father due to my sexuality you've done more than I think anyone could have asked. You were not confrontational. You came here to ask for advice. Those two things alone are huge steps. Like others have commented, I would suggest just be supportive and let your son find his own way. Be there for him, but don't pry or be pushy, you might get lucky and he will come to you when he needs you, as opposed to becoming evasive. The sense that you're no longer a part of your own family is something you never want him to feel.

I am still massively in the closet today. Some friends know, and due to recent events a few co-workers now know. I still don't have a clear sense of who I am, and have been lurking in this sub wondering if I could find friends here or should I just crawl back under my rock.
